output.summary: Deterministic verdict: FAIL; advice does not change it. The run-intersection policy window reported business_verdict FAIL, resource_verdict FAIL, and verdict FAIL. All 2,471 recorded errors are grouped as frontend.request_error, and only the checkout transaction recorded errors (2,471 of 6,717 samples); all other transactions recorded 0 errors. Resource side: the paymentservice cpu-throttle-ratio SLA check FAILed (threshold 0.2, observed max 1) across 7 cells from 1790630565000 to 1790630670000, even though absolute paymentservice CPU usage was low (mean 0.0108 cores). The error timeline (1790630540673-1790630663409) and the throttle-violation window overlap in time, but clock_alignment is not_verified_by_core, so no ordering or causal link is asserted. Recommended operator actions: verify clocks, inspect the recorded error documents and checkout flow, review paymentservice CPU quota/throttling, and rerun to re-evaluate the same policy checks.

hypotheses.recommended_check: Re-evaluate the same overall-errors rule against the identical 38,628-sample denominator and run-intersection window, and confirm run_validity VALID and analysis_coverage COMPLETE still hold for that window before rerunning.

hypotheses.observation: All 2,471 recorded errors are grouped as frontend.request_error (first_epoch_ms 1790630540673, last_epoch_ms 1790630663409), and the checkout transaction summary shows 2,471 errors out of 6,717 samples, while add product to cart, cart, home, product, and reset cart each record 0 errors (6,717 samples each except home with 6,721).
hypotheses.possible_explanation: The failed requests originated from the checkout portion of the workload and were surfaced by the frontend; which downstream step or condition produced these errors is not evidenced.
hypotheses.recommended_check: Inspect the sampled error documents in the error log, then map each frontend.request_error to the corresponding JMeter checkout sampler and checkout service steps to identify the exact failing request.

hypotheses.observation: The paymentservice cpu-throttle-ratio SLA check FAILs (operator gt, threshold 0.2), with a finding of 7 cells from 1790630565000 to 1790630670000 (observed max 1, min 0.522390289979), while paymentservice cpu_cores usage is low (mean 0.0108, max 0.0163) and the throttle-ratio series has q95 = 1.
hypotheses.possible_explanation: paymentservice may be configured with a very small CPU quota so it is throttled heavily even though absolute CPU usage is low (e.g., CFS quota exhaustion); this is a configuration hypothesis, not a proven cause of the request errors.
hypotheses.recommended_check: Compare paymentservice CPU limit/request (quota) settings with the throttled cells, inspect the 15s-resolution throttle counters, and rerun with a higher quota to see whether the throttle-ratio cells and the error rate both change.

hypotheses.recommended_check: First verify clock alignment among JMeter sampler timestamps, Prometheus metrics, and the error index; only then compare the two series in aligned 15s bins before interpreting any ordering.
